title: Establishment of a national registry for the evaluation and improvement of risk-adjusted prevention for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer
summary:
The HerediCaRe registry serves the long-term documentation of genetic and clinical data from the routine care of families with a hereditary predisposition to breast and ovarian cancer who are cared for in one of the centres of the German Consortium for Hereditary Breast and Ovarian Cancer or in the cooperating certified cancer centres. The establishment and implementation of this registry takes place in consideration of the basic data protection regulation in cooperation with certified cancer centres, a centre for documentation and biostatistics at the University of Leipzig, the statutory health insurance funds, the German Cancer Society (DKG) and the self-help group BRCA-Network. In order to answer open questions about the development and course of hereditary cancers, information about the constellation of cancers within the family and information about the presence of risk factors for cancer are documented. In addition, data on general health and health status as well as on early detection and follow-up examinations are recorded and scientifically evaluated. Furthermore, DNA from a blood sample of the patient, a so-called biosample, is also obtained and stored within the framework of the registry. The DNA is used for a molecular genetic examination and the result of the genetic analysis is also documented and used for scientific questions. 
A structured analysis of the collected data should provide detailed information on previously unanswered questions such as: 1. what are the age-specific disease rates and the natural course of disease of different genetic tumour subtypes? 2. what are the long-term clinical benefits and harms of preventive and therapeutic interventions? 3. how good are the quality of care and quality of life as well as the safety of medical treatment for those seeking advice and patients?

interventions.name: patients and individuals with a genetic predisposition for breast and/or ovarian cancer

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- fulfilled clinical inclusion criteria for a hereditary burden of breast and/or ovarian cancer
- Pathogenic germline variant detected in the familiy
- Relevance to therapy (e.g. PARPi)
- Needed from another medical point of view
Exclusion criteria:
None of the above criteria fulfilled
